is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles funestus s.s. (page 2, Results).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for GSTe2 L119F (page 3, Table 2) and Rdl A296S (page 4, Association between A296S-RDL mutation and Plasmodium infection).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 (page 3) provides genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) for L119F-GSTe2 in Obout and Mibellon.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in Obout and Mibellon, Cameroon (page 9, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study investigating the association between resistance markers and Plasmodium infection.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies collection sites as Obout (Southern Region) and Mibellon (Adamaoua Region), Cameroon (page 9, Methods).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were performed in May 2016 and February 2017 (page 9, Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new field collections and genotyping.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and bioassay data are provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study investigates the association between the L119F-GSTe2 metabolic resistance marker and Plasmodium infection in field-collected Anopheles funestus s.s. from two sites in Cameroon (Obout and Mibellon). It also examines the A296S-RDL target-site mutation. The study finds that homozygous resistant 119F/F mosquitoes are significantly more likely to be infected with Plasmodium sporozoites in Obout.
